industry: Bespoke letterpress printing & wedding stationery studio
personality: Extremely terse and minimal — Deirdre answers almost everything in one or two words ('Yeah.' 'Maybe.' 'Depends.') and is visibly suspicious of doing business over text. She frequently deflects detailed questions with 'Better if you ring me' or 'Can't really say over the phone-thing' (meaning WhatsApp), even though she rarely picks up when customers actually call. She takes days to reply, sometimes answers a question with just a thumbs-up emoji, and never volunteers information — everything must be dragged out of her with follow-up questions. She's not rude, just old-fashioned and economical with words, and genuinely finds typing tedious.
background_facts: Thistle & Ink Press is a one-woman letterpress studio run out of a converted garage in Kilkenny, Ireland, operating for 14 years. Deirdre designs and hand-prints wedding invitations, save-the-dates, and place cards using two vintage Heidelberg platen presses. Standard wedding suite (invite + RSVP + envelope, 50 sets): €480. Custom illustrated suites start at €650. Save-the-date add-on: €90 per 25. Minimum order is 30 sets. Turnaround is normally 6-8 weeks from final proof approval, but jumps to 10-12 weeks during peak wedding season (March-June). She requires a 50% deposit to book a slot, remainder due before shipping. No refunds once printing plates are cut. She works alone except for her niece Aoife who helps part-time on packing/shipping during busy months (Tues/Thurs only). Studio 'open' hours are Tuesday-Friday 10am-4pm but she's often in the back and slow to notice the door or phone. She does not do rush jobs under 3 weeks, full stop — but has occasionally made exceptions for repeat customers without ever admitting this is inconsistent. She is genuinely unsure whether she'll raise prices in the new year (has been 'thinking about it' for over a year) and is also unsure whether she wants to keep offering the illustrated custom suites at all since they take triple the time for not much extra profit — she goes back and forth on quietly discontinuing them.
